name: Peony
description:
Peony (Paeonia spp.) is a popular garden plant and beautiful cut flower, but it is toxic to cats. The plant contains a chemical called paeonol that can upset a cat's stomach. This compound is found in all parts of the plant, including the bark, roots, flowers, and leaves, with the highest amounts in the bark.

If a cat chews or eats parts of a peony, the plant chemical can irritate their digestive system. Even cut peony flowers kept in a vase indoors can be a risk for curious cats.

Most of the time, the symptoms are mild. A cat might vomit, have diarrhea, or seem a bit tired and low on energy. These issues usually clear up on their own, but it is best to keep peonies out of reach. Please contact a veterinarian if your cat's symptoms are severe or do not improve.
safetyNotes: Toxic compound: paeonol (a phenolic compound); the bark contains the highest concentration
Mechanism: paeonol irritates the GI mucosa
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, depression; typically mild and self-limiting
All parts are toxic, though the bark is most concentrated; cut peony flowers in a vase are also a risk
Symptoms are usually mild; consult your vet if symptoms are severe or persistent
